guides.explanation_en: 明るい describes a place or thing that has plenty of light and is easy to see. The light may come from the sun or from lamps.

のだ follows a clause and presents its content as an explanation or makes it salient as the basis for a statement. の packages the clause as content, and だ asserts it in this explanatory frame; after nouns and な-adjectives, な comes before のだ.

parts.contribution_en: Packages the preceding clause as content for the explanatory statement.
Asserts that content within the explanatory frame.

guides.explanation_en: つまらない describes something that does not hold your interest; it means boring or uninteresting.
決める means to decide something or settle on a choice. It can also mean to determine or set something, such as a rule or value.
回る（まわる）means to turn or spin, or to go around. In 目が回る, the image of spinning describes the sensation of dizziness, so the expression means “to feel dizzy.”
間（あいだ）means the space separating people or things, and also an interval of time. In 人の間 or 三日の間, it refers to the space or span between the things or times named.
這い出す means to get out of a place by crawling. The first part supplies the crawling action, and 出す adds movement out from inside or from a confined place.

parts.contribution_en: The linking form of 這う, “crawl”; it supplies the way of moving.
Adds movement out from inside or a confined place.

guides.explanation_en: その後 means “after that” or “afterward.” その points to an event or time already identified, and 後 means the time following it; together they refer to what comes afterward.

parts.contribution_en: Points to an event or time already identified.
Means the time following that event or time.

guides.explanation_en: 時節 combines 時, “time,” with 節, a temporal juncture or season. It can mean a fitting occasion—a juncture suitable for something—or a broader period, including an era; the word has a somewhat formal tone.

parts.contribution_en: time
a temporal juncture or season

guides.explanation_en: 話し方 combines 話す, “to speak,” in the form 話し with 方（かた）, “way” or “manner.” It means the way someone speaks.

parts.contribution_en: The continuative form of 話す, “to speak,” which combines with 方 to name a way of doing the action.
かた means a way or manner of doing the action.

guides.explanation_en: 動き出す uses 動く (“move”) in its 連用形, 動き, before 出す, which in this pattern marks the beginning of an action or movement. Together they mean “to start moving”; 出す here marks the onset, not something physically coming out.

parts.contribution_en: Move; the 連用形 of 動く used before 出す.
In this pattern, mark the beginning of an action or movement.

guides.explanation_en: 英文 (えいぶん) means text written in English, including an English composition. 英 identifies English as the language, and 文 contributes the sense of written text or composition.

parts.contribution_en: English; identifies the language.
Written text or composition.

guides.explanation_en: 勝つ means to win or prevail over something. It applies to contests and to overcoming a force, obstacle, or urge.
バイオリン is the Japanese word for a violin, a bowed string instrument.
呼ぶ means to call someone or summon them, usually to get them to come or respond. It can refer to calling out or otherwise asking someone to come.
音（おと）means a sound that can be heard, whether pleasant or unwanted. It refers broadly to audible sound, including noise.

見せる means to show something to someone, or to present someone or something as having a particular quality or appearance. In the second use, the subject shapes the impression others get; it can therefore mean “make oneself appear” or “pretend to be.”
おれ means “I” or “me” in informal speech. It is strongly associated with masculine usage and can sound blunt or familiar, so it is generally used in casual relationships rather than polite situations.
ぷうぷう is a sound-symbolic adverb for repeated soft whistling or puffing sounds. It can describe air or smoke coming out with a light, airy sound.
違う means “to differ” or “to be unlike.” It describes a person, thing, or state that is not the same as another.
絵 (え) means a picture, drawing, or painting: a visual depiction made with lines, shapes, or color.

と frames the preceding phrase or clause as content, and いう presents it as something expressed. こと turns that content into an abstract noun phrase, so the whole construction refers to a fact or notion and can fill a noun phrase position.

parts.contribution_en: Marks the preceding content as quoted or stated material.
Presents the content marked by と as something expressed.
Turns the preceding content into an abstract matter or proposition.

investigation_questions.question: Is 子 in this word functioning synchronically as a suffix-like element, a spelling element, or both?

guides.explanation_en: 様子 names the observable condition or appearance of something. 様 contributes the notion of state or appearance, while 子 is read す here and has no substantial semantic contribution.

parts.contribution_en: Contributes the notion of state or appearance.
Read す here; it has no substantial semantic contribution.

sources.title: 様子（読み）ヨウス — コトバンク（デジタル大辞泉・精選版 日本国語大辞典）
sources.summary_en: The dictionaries define 様子 as, among other senses, an observable state or condition, and also list appearance, demeanor, signs, and circumstances. Both identify 子 read as su as a 唐音 or 唐宋音. The National Language Dictionary records a 13th-century sense ‘form/model’ and a 15th-century attestation for ‘state/condition’; these entries document usage, not the word’s derivation.

sources.title: 「ようす」ということばは、どうして「様子」と書くのですか？ — 漢字文化資料館（大修館書店）
sources.summary_en: This pre-2008 article says 様 alone is enough for the meaning of 様子 and 子 has no substantial semantic contribution. It treats 子 as a suffix-like element in Chinese that adjusts the sound and identifies su as 唐音. It further asserts that 様子 shows traces of import from modern Chinese; the page does not establish the precise historical route, so that assertion is not treated as proven derivation.

sources.title: ヨウス — 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Under the head character 様, this dictionary lists 様子 senses including visible state, appearance, circumstances, signs, and demeanor, and notes 容子 as an alternative spelling. It supports word-level sense coverage, not an independent historical analysis of the two characters.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 様子 means an observable state or condition. The reference article specifically says 様 alone is sufficient for the word’s meaning; this supports explaining 様 as contributing the state/appearance notion, while treating the full word’s meaning as established lexically rather than as a compositional translation.

In 様子, 子 is read su, identified in the dictionaries as 唐音/唐宋音. The opened reference says 子 has no substantial semantic contribution in this word. The sources do not support glossing it as ‘child’ or assigning it an independent Japanese grammatical meaning; the article’s suffix-like explanation is an account of its role, not proof of the word’s exact historical formation.

The older Taishukan article says 様子 bears traces of import from modern Chinese, while the opened dictionaries identify the reading of 子 and give Japanese historical attestations. These materials do not establish a precise derivation or borrowing route. The modern-Chinese-import assertion therefore remains a source-reported hypothesis rather than a verified origin.

guides.explanation_en: は marks a phrase as the topic of a statement, roughly “as for” that phrase. By setting it apart as the topic, it can also suggest a contrast with other possible topics. It attaches to a phrase and does not itself name an object or action.

読みかける joins the continuative stem 読み (“read”) with かける, which marks an action as started but unfinished. It means to start reading something and leave it unread to the end; 読みかけの本 is a book someone has started but not finished reading.

parts.contribution_en: Continuative stem of 読む, “read.”
Marks the reading as started but unfinished.

guides.explanation_en: 捕る means to catch or capture an animal. This spelling of とる marks that sense; the verb itself does not need to be divided into smaller meaning parts.
会う means to meet or see someone, typically by being together in person. It can describe an arranged meeting or an encounter.
怒る（おこる）means to become angry or to be angry.
歩き出す combines the continuative form of 歩く, “to walk,” with 出す. After a verb, 出す marks the start of an action, so 歩き出す means “to start walking” or “to begin to walk.”

parts.contribution_en: Continuative form of 歩く, “to walk.”
After a verb, marks the start of an action.

guides.explanation_en: 一度 means “one time,” and も adds emphasis. With a negative predicate, 一度も means that not even one occasion occurred, or “never.”

parts.contribution_en: “One time”; identifies a single occasion.
With a negative predicate, emphasizes that not even one occasion occurred.

guides.explanation_en: 歩く (あるく) means “to walk; move on foot.”
だということ takes a statement ending in だ, marks it as content with という, and packages it as a fact or matter with こと. It means “the fact that …” or simply “that …”.

parts.contribution_en: Marks the preceding description as an assertion with the copula.
Marks the preceding statement as content being stated or understood.
Packages that content as a fact or matter that can be referred to.

guides.explanation_en: 今日（きょう）means “today,” the day that includes the present moment. 今 contributes “current,” and 日 contributes “day”; together they name the present day. It commonly marks when an action happens.

parts.contribution_en: Contributes the sense of what is current or present.
Contributes “day.”

guides.explanation_en: ろく describes something as decent, satisfactory, or worth having—good enough by ordinary standards. Before a noun it takes な, as in ろくなもの, and is especially common in negative statements to mean that there is no decent or adequate one.
今（いま）means the present time: “now” or “at present.”
捕まえる means to catch or seize someone or something, bringing it under your control, often by taking hold of it.
真ん中 means the middle or center. 真ん adds the sense of being right in the middle, and 中 means the middle or interior.

parts.contribution_en: Prefix-like 真ん marks the position as the exact middle; ん is part of this form, not a separate meaning.
Means the middle or interior.

guides.explanation_en: 尻（しり）means the buttocks, the rear part of the body that a person sits on.
時（とき）means a time, moment, or occasion when something happens. It is a noun; その時 means “that time.”

そのうえ connects a further point to what has already been mentioned, meaning “moreover” or “in addition.” Literally “on top of that,” it uses the image of placing one thing above another to present more information on top of an existing point.

parts.contribution_en: “That”; points back to the matter already mentioned.
“Above” or “on top”; with その, gives the image of adding a further point on top of what was already mentioned.

guides.explanation_en: 家族 (かぞく) means family: people connected as family members, often considered together as a household. 家 contributes the family or household idea, while 族 presents them as a group.

parts.contribution_en: family or household
group of people

guides.explanation_en: 持ち上げる combines the stem of 持つ, “hold,” with 上げる, “raise.” The first suggests taking hold of or supporting something, and the second gives the upward movement: to lift something up.

parts.contribution_en: The stem of 持つ contributes holding or supporting something.
Contributes moving something upward, giving the whole verb its meaning of lifting it up.

guides.explanation_en: 爪 (つめ) means the hard covering at the tip of a finger or toe; for an animal, it can mean a claw.
動き始める combines 動く (うごく, “move”) with 始める (はじめる, “begin”). The first verb supplies the action, and 始める marks its beginning, so 動き始める means “begin to move” or “start moving.”

parts.contribution_en: The connective form of 動く, supplying the action “move.”
“Begin”; after a verb, it marks the start of that action.

investigation_questions.question: What contribution, if any, did 邪 make in the earliest uses of 邪魔?
Did 魔 contribute its own meaning in the earliest compound, or mainly represent part of a Buddhist transcription?

guides.explanation_en: 邪魔 means an obstruction or interference that gets in the way of something. The broader hindrance sense is historically connected to a Buddhist use for a demon or impediment to Buddhist practice, giving a bridge from obstructing practice to hindering a goal. The contribution of each character to the older compound is not fully settled.
guides.caveat_en: Accounts differ on whether 魔 contributed meaning as a character in the older compound.

parts.contribution_en: One account reads it as adding the idea of something wrong or improper in the older Buddhist term; this contribution is not firmly established.
Buddhist usage associates it with demons and obstacles to awakening, providing historical background for the hindrance sense; its independent contribution in 邪魔 is disputed.

sources.title: 邪魔（読み）ジャマ | コトバンク: デジタル大辞泉・精選版 日本国語大辞典・普及版 字通
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen lists the general hindrance sense first and marks the Buddhist sense as the 原義 (original sense). 精選版 日本国語大辞典 defines that Buddhist sense as a wicked demon or impediment to Buddhist practice, cites 色葉字類抄 (1177–81), and records a general hindrance use in 虎寛本狂言・煎物 (late Muromachi to early modern period). These entries support the historical senses and attestations; they do not by themselves demonstrate the compound’s morphology or independently establish each character’s contribution.

sources.title: 魔（読み）マ | コトバンク: デジタル大辞泉・精選版 日本国語大辞典・普及版 字通・ブリタニカ国際大百科事典
sources.summary_en: Digital Daijisen and 精選版 日本国語大辞典 describe 魔 as an abbreviation of 魔羅, a transcription of Sanskrit māra, and give Buddhist meanings involving a demon or obstruction to awakening. 字通 describes the character as made to transcribe māra. This supports the historical Buddhist association of 魔 with obstruction and demon imagery, but does not prove that 魔 independently contributes that meaning in modern 邪魔.

sources.title: 邪魔 | じつは身近な仏教用語 | 日蓮宗ポータルサイト
sources.summary_en: The Nichiren-shū page describes 邪魔 as originally a demon obstructing awakening and says 魔 was created to represent the sound ma in a transcription of māra, without meaning as a character in that transcription. This is one religious explanation of the older term and conflicts with the component interpretation in the Ōtani University page.

sources.title: 邪魔 | 生活の中の仏教用語 | 大谷大学
sources.summary_en: A Shin Buddhist studies professor says 邪魔 originally referred to a 魔 that hindered Buddhist teaching and practice, with 邪 adding the sense of “not right.” The article connects the modern hindrance sense to things that frustrate a goal. This is an explicit component interpretation, not independent proof of a historical derivation.

claims.text_en: Japanese dictionary entries attest both a Buddhist sense of 邪魔, involving a demon or something that obstructs Buddhist practice, and a broader sense of hindrance. 精選版 日本国語大辞典 cites 色葉字類抄 (1177–81) for the Buddhist sense and a late-medieval to early-modern kyōgen text for a general hindrance use; Digital Daijisen labels the Buddhist sense as the 原義.

The Buddhist association of 魔 with demons and obstacles is historically relevant: Japanese dictionaries describe 魔 as an abbreviation of 魔羅, a transcription of Sanskrit māra, and include Buddhist meanings such as an impediment to awakening. This supports a historical bridge from Buddhist obstruction to the general hindrance sense, but does not show that 魔 independently supplies the full modern meaning in every use.

Accounts disagree about the characters’ semantic contributions. Ōtani University explains 邪 as adding a sense of “not right,” while Nichiren-shū says 魔 is a sound-bearing character in the transcription and contributes no meaning there. These explanations do not establish a settled component-by-component derivation of modern 邪魔.

The evil-demon association has dictionary support as historical background for the Buddhist sense. In the supplied sentence, however, 邪魔 means interference with sketching; the dictionary evidence does not justify reading the modern occurrence literally as an evil or troublesome force.

guides.explanation_en: つるつる evokes a surface that is smoothly even, often with a glossy look. Adding する makes this quality into a verb: つるつるする means to be or feel smooth and sometimes glossy.

Turns the quality into a verb meaning to be or feel that way.

guides.explanation_en: After a number or quantity, ほど marks an approximate amount, as in 三日ほど, “about three days.” After a phrase, it marks the degree something reaches, often with a result or comparison; in Aほど～ない, the negative says that nothing is as ～ as A. In ～ば～ほど, it links two changes to mean “the more ..., the more ...”.

investigation_questions.question: What evidence establishes 分’s contribution to the older ‘one’s share or due portion’ sense, beyond the compatible character meaning?

guides.explanation_en: 随分 means ‘quite,’ ‘very,’ or ‘considerably,’ marking a high degree. Japanese use developed from concrete quantity to abstract degree; it can also suggest that the degree is striking, sometimes with surprise or dissatisfaction. Older records include a sense related to one’s due share, but the modern degree meaning is not built by adding separate character meanings.
guides.caveat_en: The older analysis relates 随 to ‘follow’ and 分 to ‘share’ or ‘status.’ The evidence does not establish distinct contributions from these characters to the modern degree meaning.

parts.contribution_en: In an older analysis, this means ‘follow’ or ‘accord with’ in relation to a share; its contribution to the modern degree meaning is not established.
In the older sense, this is compatible with ‘share’ or ‘status’; a distinct contribution to the modern degree meaning is not established.

sources.title: 随分（読み）ズイブン — コトバンク; デジタル大辞泉 and 精選版 日本国語大辞典
sources.summary_en: The dictionaries record a noun sense ‘in keeping with one’s status or due portion,’ with a cited example dated circa 892; an adverbial sense ‘as much as one can’ cited to the early 13th century; and a degree-adverb sense ‘greatly, considerably, very,’ with an example from the early 13th century. sources.summary_en: The entries record 分 with senses including a divided share or portion, a person’s status or capacity, and an amount or degree. claims.text_en: Japanese dictionaries record both an older noun sense of 随分 meaning ‘in keeping with one’s status or due portion’ and later adverb senses, including ‘as much as one can’ and ‘greatly/considerably/very.’ Their dated citations include circa 892 for the noun sense and early-13th-century examples for the adverb senses. The citations document recorded uses; they should not alone be presented as proof of a continuous step-by-step derivation.

Narumi’s scholarly study analyzes the Japanese development of 随分’s degree meaning as proceeding through a concrete quantity-adverb use, followed by abstract degree meaning and then evaluative meaning. This supplies a scholarly account of the bridge to modern ‘quite/very/considerably’; the modern degree use is not explained by simply adding character glosses.

The study discusses an older ‘according to one’s share/lot’ interpretation, and the Japanese dictionaries record a compatible older noun sense. The characters also have relevant standalone glosses: 随 can mean ‘follow,’ while 分 can mean ‘share/portion’ or ‘status.’ These facts make ‘分に随う’ an intelligible historical segmentation, but do not establish that the modern degree adverb retains separate, productive meanings for each component.

For the supplied example, 痩せている is modified by the degree-adverb sense of 随分. Digital Daijisen defines this use as ‘very/greatly/considerably’ and notes that it often carries a reaction such as surprise or dissatisfaction; the dictionary wording describes a tendency, not a required nuance in every occurrence.

前 (まえ) refers to the front or area ahead of a reference point. For time or sequence, it refers to what came earlier, before that point.
初めて (はじめて) means that something happens or is experienced on its first occasion. It commonly frames a verb or clause, and can modify a noun in phrases such as 初めての経験 (a first experience).

書 points to books or study, while 生 identifies a learner, as in 学生. Together, 書生 means a student engaged in study; in Japanese usage it often refers to a young man lodging in someone else’s home while studying.

parts.contribution_en: Points to books or study.
Identifies a learner or student.

guides.explanation_en: 通る means to pass through a place or go across a space. With を, it can mark the place or route that the movement traverses.
筋向（すじむかい）means “across the street” or “opposite,” usually of a place. 筋 refers to a street or route, and 向 indicates the facing or opposite side; together they describe a location across that street.

parts.contribution_en: street or route that serves as the reference
the facing or opposite side

guides.explanation_en: 昼寝 combines 昼, “daytime,” with 寝, “sleeping,” to mean sleep taken during the day: a nap.

parts.contribution_en: daytime
sleeping

guides.explanation_en: たいへん means “very” or “extremely.” It is used before an adjective or other expression to emphasize its degree, as in たいへん強い, “very strong.”
守る (まもる) means to keep someone or something safe, or to keep to a rule by following it. In both uses, something is kept from being harmed or violated.
有名 means famous or well-known. 有 contributes “have,” and 名 means “name”: the image of having a name people know extends to being famous. It modifies nouns with な and can be used predicatively with だ.

parts.contribution_en: Contributes “have” in the image of having a name.
Means “name,” the basis for being known.

guides.explanation_en: 現れる means to appear or emerge: to come into view or become present. It is used for people, things, and phenomena.
後ろ means the back part of something or the area behind it. It refers to the rear side or the space extending from that side.
Sentence-final な marks a speaker’s observation or adds emphasis to a remark. Depending on intonation and context, it can sound exclamatory or like a thought voiced to oneself.
上手になる means “become skilled” or “get good at something.” 上手 means skillful, and になる marks becoming that way; the skill or activity can be named with が, as in 英語が上手になる.

parts.contribution_en: skillful; good at something
marks the state someone becomes
become

guides.explanation_en: 縁側 is a veranda running along the side of a Japanese room. 縁 points to the room’s edge, and 側 places the veranda alongside it.

parts.contribution_en: the room’s edge
the side alongside that edge

guides.explanation_en: 向こう means “the other side” or “a place over there,” viewed as across from or beyond a reference point. The exact location depends on context.
元気 means the vitality or energy that supports feeling well and being active. In everyday speech, it is also used to ask or say whether someone is doing well.

parts.contribution_en: Suggests a basis or source.
Contributes the sense of vitality or energy.

guides.explanation_en: 変になる means to become strange or take on an unusual state. 変 describes that state, and に links it as the result of the change marked by なる.

parts.contribution_en: strange; unusual
marks 変 as the state that results
become; come to be

guides.explanation_en: 三枚 combines the number 三 (さん, “three”) with 枚 (まい), the counter for flat, thin objects. It means “three flat objects”; the object being counted is understood from context.

parts.contribution_en: “Three”; gives the quantity.
Counter for flat, thin objects; indicates what kind of thing is counted.

guides.explanation_en: 一円 means an amount of one yen. 一 gives the number one, and 円 names the yen unit of money.

parts.contribution_en: one
the yen unit of money

guides.explanation_en: 鳴く means for an animal to make a sound, such as meowing, barking, or calling. The particular sound varies with the animal.
怒り（いかり） means anger, the strong displeasure someone feels. It is used as a noun in expressions such as 怒りを感じる (“feel anger”).
それ refers to a time or point already understood, and まで marks it as the endpoint of a span. Together, それまで means “until then” or “up to that time.”

parts.contribution_en: refers to a time or point already understood
marks the endpoint of a span; with a time reference, “until” or “up to”

guides.explanation_en: 天気 means weather: conditions in the sky and surrounding air. 天 points to the sky, while 気 contributes the sense of air or atmosphere; together they name atmospheric conditions.

parts.contribution_en: sky
air or atmosphere

guides.explanation_en: 見るなり combines 見る, “see,” with なり, which marks the next action as happening immediately after the seeing. It means “as soon as someone sees something.”

parts.contribution_en: the seeing that the next action immediately follows
marks the next action as happening immediately after the preceding action

guides.explanation_en: 五つ counts five items without specifying their kind. It can also state that someone is five years old.

parts.contribution_en: Supplies the number five.
The native general counter suffix, used when no specific item counter is named.

guides.explanation_en: 尋ねる means to ask or inquire, usually by putting a question to someone to get information or an answer.

investigation_questions.question: Does 椽 contribute a live rafter-related meaning in 椽側, or is it only an alternate spelling of 縁側?

guides.explanation_en: 椽側, also written 縁側, is a board-floored area outside the rooms of a traditional house, running along its side and serving as a passage or entrance. 側 indicates its position along the house; the sources do not establish that 椽 adds a rafter meaning in this word.

parts.contribution_en: Its contribution in this word is unresolved; the character can mean “rafter” independently.
Indicates the space's position along the side of the house.

sources.title: 縁側（読み）エンガワ | コトバンク
sources.summary_en: The entry in 精選版 日本国語大辞典 lists 縁側・椽側・縁頬 as written forms for えんがわ. Its architectural sense is a board-floored area outside rooms in a house, also used as a passage or entrance; it gives a late-17th-century example. The same page's encyclopedia entries describe exterior and interior-facing forms and their architectural history. It does not explain the spelling 椽側 or the word's etymology.

sources.title: 椽 | 漢字一字 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Defines 椽 as たるき: a round timber laid from the ridge to the eaves to support the roof. This establishes a rafter sense for the character, not a contribution to 椽側.

sources.title: 垂木（読み）タルキ | コトバンク
sources.summary_en: The デジタル大辞泉 entry lists 椽 among the written forms of たるき and defines the item as a long timber running from the ridge toward the eaves to support a roof. The encyclopedia entry describes its structural role in a roof. Neither entry analyzes 椽側.

sources.title: 縁側 | 用語集 | 日本の文化遺産を探す
sources.summary_en: Defines 縁側 as a narrow board-floored space outside a sitting room, between the house and garden, used as a passage or a place to sit. It distinguishes a rain-exposed 縁 as 濡縁 and describes terminology for other features. It does not discuss 椽側.

sources.title: 縁側／えんがわ - 語源由来辞典
sources.summary_en: Proposes that 縁側 is a mixed Sino-Japanese compound: it says 縁 means an edge or border and is also written 椽, while 側 is a native Japanese word for the surrounding area. The page offers no supporting historical attestations or citations for this analysis, which does not establish why 椽側 is used or that 椽 contributes 'rafter' to the compound.

sources.title: 縁側｜建築士用語辞書 | 東建コーポレーション
sources.summary_en: Gives an architectural account in which an exterior board-floored 縁 became enclosed within the building when doors divided it from the outside, yielding 縁側; it calls the exterior form 濡れ縁. This is a general architectural explanation and does not address the 椽側 spelling or document the word's historical derivation.

sources.title: 縁側の起源，本来の役割を調べたい | レファレンス協同データベース
sources.summary_en: A library reference response lists specialist books and articles for researching the origin and historical role of 縁側. It identifies relevant references, including a dictionary entry for えん・縁・椽, but does not provide their contents or an etymological conclusion.

claims.text_en: Kanjipedia defines 椽 as a round roof-supporting rafter, and the Kotobank entry for 垂木 also lists 椽 as a written form of たるき. These sources support 'rafter' as a meaning of the character in that context, not 'eaves' themselves.

精選版 日本国語大辞典 records 椽側 as a spelling of えんがわ and defines the architectural word as a board-floored area outside rooms that can also serve as a passage or entrance. It does not say that 椽 has a distinct or productive rafter meaning in this word.

The reviewed sources do not establish a derivation from rafters to a veranda or corridor. One general etymology website analyzes the spelling through 縁 ('edge') plus 側 ('side/area'), but it supplies no historical evidence for that account or for why 椽 is used in 椽側.

縁側 is used for spaces with differing positions and boundaries: the encyclopedia describes both exterior and interior-facing forms, while the heritage glossary describes a space between sitting room and garden and distinguishes an exposed wet edge as 濡縁. The sources do not document a meaning or usage distinction between the spellings 椽側 and 縁側.

An architectural glossary presents an account in which an exterior 縁 becomes enclosed by doors and is then called 縁側. This offers context for the architectural term, but it is not evidence for the word's historical derivation or for the spelling 椽側.

The opened dictionary records a late-17th-century example of 縁側, but it does not establish the history of the 椽側 spelling or a transition from a rafter-related sense to the architectural meaning.

guides.explanation_en: 合わせる means to bring things together or adjust them so they line up. It is used when someone brings separate things into alignment or makes them fit together.

investigation_questions.question: Does historical or linguistic evidence establish a distinct “part” or “share” contribution from 分 in 自分?

guides.explanation_en: 自分 means oneself or one’s own, and is also used as a first-person “I.” Which person it refers to depends on the sentence.
guides.caveat_en: The available evidence does not establish a separate current meaning for 分 within 自分.

sources.title: 自分／じぶん - 語源由来辞典
sources.summary_en: The entry asserts that 分 in 自分 is the 分 in 本分, glossed there as an innate quality; it says 自分 referred to one's own ability and was also used for 'I myself.' It gives no dated examples, citations, or derivational evidence for that account.

sources.title: 「自分」の再帰的な用法に関する考察
sources.summary_en: This 2025 Hokkaido University paper studies modern grammatical behavior of 自分. It discusses reflexive, viewpoint, logophoric, first-person singular, and dialectal addressee uses; it does not examine a meaning contribution from 分 or the word's derivation.

sources.title: 自分（読み）ジブン - コトバンク
sources.summary_en: The page reproduces entries from Digital Daijisen and the Nihon Kokugo Daijiten. They define 自分 as the person themself/self and record first-person uses; the Nihon Kokugo Daijiten gives cited historical examples, including a 1425 first-person example. These dictionary entries do not analyze 分 as a live component meaning 'part/share.'

claims.text_en: 語源由来辞典 proposes that 分 in 自分 is related to 本分 and says 自分 referred to one's own ability before also being used for 'I myself.' This is an assertion by that reference, not a derivation established by evidence presented on the opened page.

The opened Japanese dictionary entries define 自分 as oneself/the person themself and also record first-person 'I' uses. The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten entry gives historical citations, including a first-person example dated 1425; these support historical use, but do not establish that 分 contributes a current compositional 'own part/share' meaning.
A 2025 scholarly study describes several grammatical uses of modern 自分, including reflexive and first-person uses, but does not address 分's semantic contribution or the word's historical derivation.

guides.explanation_en: こと treats the preceding clause as an event or situation; さえ emphasizes that even this occurs. With ある, the phrase means that such an event happens on some occasions, often presenting it as unexpected or notable.

parts.contribution_en: Turns the preceding clause into an event or situation that can be treated as a case.
Adds “even,” emphasizing that this event or situation occurs.
Says that such an event or situation occurs on some occasions.

guides.explanation_en: どちら asks which of two alternatives is meant. It directs attention to the choice between them.

実 points to what is real, while 際 contributes the sense of a situation or circumstances. Together 実際 means the actual state of affairs, and is used adverbially in forms such as 実際に and 実際は to mean “in fact” or “in reality.”

parts.contribution_en: what is real or actual
the situation or circumstances

guides.explanation_en: After a verb in dictionary form, うち treats the action as a span of time. It places what follows within that span, often while the action is repeated or progresses.
痛い describes pain or soreness, usually as a physical sensation. It can also describe something that hurts.

顔 means “face,” を marks it as what is brought together, and 合わせる means “bring together.” The phrase evokes bringing one person’s face together with another’s, and conventionally means to meet face-to-face.

parts.contribution_en: face
marks 顔 as what is brought together
bring together
